comment: The Qt plugins a HikariSub package carries beside the Qt libraries, per platform (docs/proposals/backend-interfaces.md: deployment manifests enumerate Qt plugins). Each entry is a plugin file name without prefix or suffix under <Qt>/plugins/<category>, the Qt module archive that provides it (checked against cmake/locks/qt-<platform>.lock.json) and why the application loads it. Checked by cmake/manifest/QtDeploymentManifest.cmake (ctest qt-deployment-manifest), which itself requires K1's imageformats/qsvg and iconengines/qsvgicon on every platform; dependency-load loads those two. The other entries are the plan for Phase 5 packaging: the check only finds each in the Qt lock and, on the platform it runs on, in the provisioned Qt; nothing yet shows the application loads it, and no package is built from this file yet. The QML modules and the Qt libraries themselves are Phase 5 packaging's.

wayland-shell-integration.why: top-level and floating panel windows on Wayland

wayland-graphics-integration-client.why: Qt Quick's OpenGL surfaces on Wayland

wayland-decoration-client.why: window frames where the compositor draws none (mutter)

platformthemes.why: the desktop's file dialogs and colour scheme through xdg-desktop-portal

imageformats.why: K1: SVG images (the Qt SVG image plugin)

iconengines.why: K1: SVG icons (the Qt SVG icon engine)

tls.why: P8: the update check's https feed

multimedia.why: the general player (Qt Multimedia's FFmpeg backend)
